cuda.reference: minfer's CUDA arm, recorded by the gate itself (the same 32-step loop)
cuda.note: #724 re-recorded: with the file's `rope_freqs.weight` table applied (llama.cpp always did; this engine did not until #724) the CUDA arm reproduces llama.cpp's 32 ids token for token. The pre-#724 record was a seven-token cycle (9822 at step 5) that #737 attributed to the f32-activation class; on CUDA it was the missing table. Step 5 is a 0.04-logit tie in every implementation measured: llama.cpp 0.0367 for 10057, CUDA now on 10057, Metal 0.0419 for 9822, the CPU 0.027 for 9822. Measured 2026-11-05 with the gate itself on the same 32-step loop.

metal.reference: minfer's Metal arm, recorded by the gate itself (the same 32-step loop)
metal.note: #723's Metal record, re-measured 2026-11-05 with #724's rope table applied: the gate still reproduces these 32 ids, and the agreeing prefix's worst top-logit |Δ| against the recorded CPU reference is 0.1735 (class tolerance 0.5). #724 moved CUDA across the step-5 tie (to llama.cpp's 10057) and left Metal on the cycle side — metal margin 0.0419 for 9822 against llama.cpp's 0.0367 for 10057 — so the cycle is a 0.04-margin coin flip of the device class, not a Metal kernel defect, and not something the rope table resolves for every backend.

rope_table.note: the file carries one global f32 table (values: fifteen 1.0, then 1.6513293, 3.2922628, 9.666731, then thirteen 32.0). llama.cpp's rope divides each pair's angle by its entry (`theta_base/freq_factor`), and #724 made this engine do the same; a run that drops the table is bit-identical only at short context, because the affected pairs rotate by <=0.05 rad over the first 32 positions.

tie.note: measured 2026-11-05: llama.cpp b11829 (184f65360) on the same file reports 10057 at logprob -1.5233 and 9822 at -1.5600 (margin 0.0367); this engine's CPU run lands on 9822 by 0.0270. Both apply the file's rope table; the ~0.064 difference is the CPU/CPU numeric class (quantized activations, accumulation order), and it is larger than llama.cpp's own margin.

cpu.note: the CPU arm is token-exact up to a near-tie that llama.cpp itself resolves by 0.037; #724's contract is that the engine follows the reference's *table*, not that it resolves every tie the same way. The 8192-token gate (scaled_reference_tokens.json) carries the exact-id claim, where the margins are not ties.

cpu_top2_note: the CPU trajectory minfer produced at the time this pin was recorded (before #724 applied the file's rope table). It is the cross-class reference the device arms check their agreeing prefix against: unscaled, it is also the trajectory llama.cpp follows, because the table moves only the low-frequency pairs and step 5 is the one place where that is worth more than the class difference.
